## Findings
- claim-1: The supplied source-29 full text states Lemma 2.5’s implication from a nonzero homogeneous syzygy to consistency of the decomposable equations, and defines tall right-hand sides as \(f_{\nu_B}\) and wide ones as \(0\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 176-189]
- claim-2: The supplied text states Theorem 4.4’s inconsistency conclusion and Theorem 4.5 derives absence of the specified syzygy from Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-502]
- claim-3: The required complete formulas for equations (8)–(10) and all Definition 2.1 valid-tuple inequalities are not recoverable from the supplied source-29 passage: its equation displays and the inequalities following “with” are corrupted/truncated. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 149-188]
- claim-4: No supplied alternate-provider FULL-TEXT SOURCE supplies an uncorrupted bounded replacement excerpt containing all requested items.
- claim-5: The requested target—one uncorrupted bounded full-text excerpt containing (8)–(10), complete Definition 2.1 inequalities, and the Lemma 2.5/Theorems 4.4–4.5 linkage—is **not established**.
## Strategy
Use the recorded ar5iv full text for limited linkage only: Lemma 2.5 at lines 176–189 and Theorems 4.4–4.5 at lines 473–502. Treat Crossref metadata and the 2011 paper as non-substitutes. Seek a native arXiv or publisher full-text extraction of source-29.

## Gaps
The sole supplied 2024 full text is corrupted at equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1 (lines 149–188). No alternate-provider 2024 full-text excerpt was retrieved. Thus the complete valid-tuple inequalities are unavailable.

“Valid \(\varphi\)” is a theorem hypothesis, but its full content cannot be stated from the corrupted passage. The branches \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\) and \(N>\min(j,n-r-i)\) in Theorem 4.4’s proof are proof-only cases, not added theorem hypotheses.

## Next
Retrieve one bounded, digested native-arXiv or publisher excerpt containing verbatim Definition 2.1, equations (8)–(10), Lemma 2.5, and Theorems 4.4–4.5. The requested target is **not established**.
